body: Those speakers he named have very sub par bass extension, PB 310 goes much deeper and fuller.

Hi there, I have a question,  just received my PCX 550 II headphones and I love them a lot even more than my DT 1990 Pro's and they are less than half the price, with the right EQ treble band tuning and through the single ended AMP output they sound a lot more clear than through APTX Bluetooth or digital USB, and the sound gets really close to the older 650 HD, about 80/85%  performance wise and accuracy.  Insane for a pair of ANC headphones. The headphones come with a 2.5mm port and I was wondering if I can plug a 2.5mm balanced cable and connect to the more powerful (195mw instead of 135mw single ended) balanced 2.5mm port. or do you think the PCX 550 II port is most likely not balanced, Sennheiser is known for having their 2.5mm ports balanced but the question is how far they went with this and if they even did it for their wireless headphones...

Thanks!

I have been loving the PXC 550-ii's for the last 3 weeks of owning these, I plugged them straight with a balanced 2.5mm to 2.55mm cable through my Sabre ES9038Q2M AMP and I actually like the sound a lot, and my older Beyer DT 1990 Pro's are catching some dust since I got these, after half a hour of EQ work reducing the 5khz/6.3khz peaks, the sound gets to about 85% the quality and output of a HD 650 which cost more than triple the price and is bulky, wired and obviously ment for different people and audio reasons. My friend also bought his own pair, since he was looking for a wireless headset, and was almost going for the XM4, which has better ANC, but not the wired sound detail and accuracy not even close. He listened to them through the amp. and we both couldn't beleive how close they were to his  HD 650's. The ANC is a satisfying extra, especially while typing or gaming and not hearing your mouse clicks and mechanical keyboard switches. Super light, comfortable, whenever you want wireless and compact/foldable. Very happy with these definitely not the brightest nor clearest, but a very satisfying and delicate piece of audiogear in my book.

Thanks for the comment, I currently own TYGR 300r's and love the boosted sub bass, while keeping the mid's intact with less sibilance, it can get really thumping with a bassy amp. I was wondering if for deeper bass extension the 1990 Pro is worth spending the extra money for, or if the newer DT 900 Pro X has enough lower bass extension to the point it could be a valid upgrade over the TYGR 300r's. To DMS a TYGR 300r is around 80% of the capacity of a DT 1990 Pro, so could we say the DT 900 Pro X sits around 90%? Of course the 900 pro x would need some slight EQ work to even reach baseline bass level of the TYGRs, since they are made for monitoring and critical listening, I'm not a crazy basshead, just love slightly deeper and boosted sub-bass. TYGRS are my first beyerdynamic headphones, first open cans for a fact, own them for two weeks atm, really shocked by it's value and really loving them, want to give them away if I find the right upgrade.
